topic: Browser restore input and resize performance
currentUserGoal: Keep the ecosystem game clickable and responsive after minimizing and maximizing the browser window.
workCompleted: Reproduced the failure with a compact-to-maximized viewport transition: the visible canvas and field hit area resized, but real Phaser canvas clicks stopped reaching the scene.
Identified the root cause in the global resize path: Phaser refreshed its pointer transform while the canvas still had the old CSS dimensions, then the canvas CSS size changed afterward.
Added a tested viewport resize helper that applies the final game and canvas CSS dimensions before Phaser refreshes its scale and pointer bounds.
Ignored hidden and transiently unusable viewport sizes so a minimized window cannot lay out the game at near-zero dimensions.
Added visibility, focus, and page-show recovery refreshes so restoring a browser resynchronizes Phaser even when the final viewport dimensions match the previous window size.
Made the ecosystem resize listener skip duplicate-size layouts, avoid preparing the hidden Memory Grove during an active run, and unregister only its own listener on shutdown.
Exported canvas bounds and pointer scale through the ecosystem playtest harness for direct regression diagnosis.
Added viewport regression tests covering CSS-before-Phaser ordering and minimized-size rejection.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 179 Vitest tests across 22 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Automated browser regression reproduced a 320x200 to 1920x1080 transition on the actual ecosystem route.
After the fix, canvas bounds were 1920x1080, pointer scale was exactly 1x1, and the 1020x882 field surface matched its 1020x882 Phaser hit area.
The first real canvas touch after maximizing was accepted with 0.0 ms reported input latency.
The maximized one-tile playtest measured 144 FPS, 6.75 ms p95 frame delta, and zero frame spikes in the sampled window.
A 390x844 phone transition also kept canvas, field surface, hit area, and touch input synchronized.
The browser console had no warnings or errors during the final checks.
git diff --check passed apart from the repository's existing Windows LF-to-CRLF notices.

gitStatus.expectedAfterCommit: Resize recovery checkpoint committed locally; master is one commit ahead of origin/master and has not been pushed.

knownIssues: The automated viewport transition exercises the same stale-bounds failure path, but a final hands-on minimize and maximize in the user's normal browser is still the best confirmation of OS-window behavior.
The game remains explicitly alpha; this slice fixes resize responsiveness and does not retune ecosystem balance.
nextRecommendedSteps: Hands-on minimize and maximize the normal ecosystem playtest once and confirm the first field click and Options button both respond immediately.
Continue the early Growth and first-expansion pacing test after resize behavior is confirmed.
Use the new canvasBounds and pointerScale harness fields for any future resize regression instead of inferring input geometry from screenshots.
doNotRevert: Do not move the canvas CSS assignments after game.scale.setParentSize; Phaser must read the final client rectangle while refreshing pointer coordinates.
Do not process hidden or near-zero viewport dimensions as real game layouts.
Do not restore the anonymous ecosystem resize listener or the broad scale.off(RESIZE) cleanup.
Do not cite the legacy 1200-tile harness as ecosystem performance evidence.
Do not touch docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
